d: The HIV enzyme that copies the viral RNA genome into DNA. It does not proofread, so it creates the mutations that drive drug resistance. NRTIs and NNRTIs both target it.
The herpes simplex and varicella-zoster enzyme that adds the first phosphate to acyclovir. Only infected cells make it, so the drug is switched on where the virus grows. Losing it causes resistance.
An empty shell that self-assembles from the HPV L1 capsid protein. The immune system sees it as the virus, but it holds no DNA, so a vaccine made from it cannot cause infection.
A mononucleosis-like illness 2 to 4 weeks after HIV infection, with fever, rash, sore throat and swollen nodes. Viral load is very high, but antibody tests may still be negative.
The DNA copy of the HIV genome that integrase inserts into a host chromosome. It is copied with the cell and hides in resting CD4 cells, which is why antiretroviral therapy must continue for life.
